title: Wildcard identity namespace overrode OpenFeature eval context
answers: Flag evaluation fails/rejected for cluster-wide service tokens
Wildcard namespace * causing OpenFeature namespace mismatch
Why does a service account with wildcard namespace break flag targeting?
body: Symptom: requests authenticated with a wildcard identity namespace (e.g. a cluster-wide service token) caused OpenFeature flag evaluation to be rejected as a namespace mismatch. Root cause: pkg/services/contexthandler/contexthandler.go:setRequestContext used id.Namespace unconditionally whenever id != nil, so "*" (or empty) propagated into the eval context, no longer matching the caller's concrete auth namespace downstream. Fix pattern: when deriving a scoping value from an identity for use by another subsystem, treat sentinel/wildcard values as "no concrete value" and fall back to a more specific default (here: stack namespace, then "default") instead of passing the sentinel through. Constraints: applies to derivations feeding external/downstream scoping systems (like OpenFeature); does not apply to authorization checks where "*" is an intentional wildcard grant.
applies: pkg/services/contexthandler and any other code deriving a scoping key from identity.Namespace for use outside the auth layer.
